reply: Guided tour of Epsilon Indi B: 6 steps. Touch any control to take over.

steps.say: This is Epsilon Indi B: Pair of brown dwarfs (T1 + T6) about 3.6 pc away, seen as a single source by SPHEREx. SPHEREx imaged it on 4 dates in D5, from 2025-05-09 to 2026-09-27 (506 days). The view starts on D5 (3.83–4.41 µm).

Play the dates in order. At 4.7″/yr it should move about 1.1 px (pixels are 6.2″) between the first and last date; the crosshair marks where the catalog motion puts it on each date. Measured between 2025-05-09 and 2026-09-27, the dates where it is bright enough to fit: 0.92 px, against 1.1 px expected for that interval.
Blink compares two dates directly: 2025-05-09 against 2026-09-27. A moving source jumps; a still one only changes brightness, if at all.

The six detectors cover 0.75–5.0 µm, from left to right. In the measurements it is detected in D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D6. Its D5/D4 flux ratio (methane index) is 3.0; ordinary stars sit near 0.5–1.5 and methane-rich cold dwarfs far above.
The model motor-rf-E_servible_binario-spherex-2026-11-16T0256 labels it a candidate cold brown dwarf; that agrees with the catalog type (cold brown dwarf, SIMBAD).
